analysis: The only change in this PR is documentation in docs/reference/configuration.md. It bumps the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and adds an 'Add-on hold' section (head lines 150-164). The section documents two env vars, DARKBLOOM_ADDON_SOCKET and DARKBLOOM_ADDON_DEV_IDENTITY, plus the lease-seconds bounds and drain/settle timeouts. It states that DARKBLOOM_ADDON_DEV_IDENTITY is read only in DEBUG builds and that neither variable is in the LaunchAgent passthrough, so the installed provider always serves the default socket. Because the diff is docs-only, no code, authorization, attestation, encryption or billing behavior changes here. Base units 4 and 5 (the SSD prefix cache and other config docs, T-041 related) are unchanged context; the head view in unit 6 covers only lines 1-307, and the head side of the add-on section is visible there. Remaining integration questions are outside the supplied evidence. They are whether AddonPeerPolicy actually enforces peer code-signing identity on the local add-on hold Unix socket, whether release builds really never read DARKBLOOM_ADDON_DEV_IDENTITY, whether the socket and ownership.lock are created with 0700/owner-only permissions, and whether a held add-on can deny service to the provider (lease bounded at 30-600s). The add-on hold IPC is a new local trust surface, and the threat model (TB-003, TB-011) does not yet mention it. The code and addon-hold-ipc.md are not supplied, so I cannot raise a finding. A later pass that sees the Addon/* sources should check them.
